The firstborn grown suddenly sensitive after a new sibling

After a second child is born, has your firstborn suddenly started throwing tantrums or acting like a baby, leaving you flustered? Perhaps your heart sank at the words "I hate my little sibling!"

This isn't because your child has turned bad — it's an expression of anxiety about losing your love. When you understand and hug the firstborn's hurt feelings, that hurt can grow into love for the little sibling.

content.alt: 39. Because I'm the Big Brother, I'll Help! - Why acknowledging the firstborn's hurt matters
content.text:
Why acknowledging the firstborn's hurt matters

A firstborn's jealousy doesn't disappear just because you suppress it. In fact, saying "You shouldn't feel that way" only makes a child lonelier.

A child whose hurt is acknowledged first gains the security of knowing they don't have to hide their feelings — and only then do they find the room to accept the new sibling. Jealousy isn't the opposite of love; it's another face of wanting to be loved.
content.caption: Jealousy isn't the opposite of love — it's the wish to be loved.

content.alt: 39. Because I'm the Big Brother, I'll Help! - Hori's story, where hurt grows into love
content.text:
Hori's story, where hurt grows into love

In Because I'm the Big Brother, I'll Help!, Hori feels as though Mom's arms are entirely taken over by the new baby, so he hides under the blanket and cries. That's when Dad says, "But there's something only a big brother can do."

When Hori hands a rattle to the crying baby, Hoya stops crying at once and giggles with delight. The hurt that had filled his heart melts away. Now Hori becomes a proper big brother who even sings lullabies. Feeling both Hori's hurt and his pride, a child learns that a little sibling is 'someone only I can love.'
content.caption: In something only a big brother can do, hurt grew into love.

content.alt: 39. Because I'm the Big Brother, I'll Help! - How to soothe the firstborn's heart at home
content.text:
How to soothe the firstborn's heart at home

First, put your child's hurt into words. Instead of "Don't be jealous," say "You missed being in Mom's arms, didn't you?" And create 'something only a big brother or big sister can do.' Small roles like handing the baby a rattle or singing a song give them pride.

When they help the little sibling, praise them big: "Thanks to you, your sibling smiled!" If you set aside even a few minutes a day just for the firstborn, your child confirms in their heart that your love hasn't shrunk.
content.caption: A big brother's own role and praise are the seeds of sibling love.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q. How should I soothe a child who's jealous of a new sibling?

A. Rather than treating the jealousy as bad, acknowledge it first and give them a hug. When you let them feel the pride of "I help because I'm the big brother," their care for the little sibling grows.

Q. Can a sibling jealousy story help?

A. By watching the main character grow close with their sibling, your child gains the feeling of having their own heart understood. Sibling jealousy stories warmly soothe the firstborn's hurt.

Q. My firstborn throws a lot of tantrums since the new baby arrived.

A. It's a wish to be reassured of your love, so set aside time just for the two of you. When you often express that they are still precious, their heart settles.
